newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's PUMA issuance to rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's PUMA issuance to rise in 1997.

text.p: PUMA Management Ltd, Macquarie Bank's mortgage securitisation vehicle, said on Wednesday its funding programme for 1997 will rise sharply to A$3.0 billion in 1997 from A$1.3 billion in 1996.
"We have increased our funding programme substantially for 1997, reflecting PUMA's and Aussie Home Loan's continued strong growth," said Tony Gill, PUMA's managing director.
PUMA announced a A$500 million four tranche offering in the domestic market today, but it expects a percentage of this year's funding to be raised offshore.

"During 1997, we expect to provide funding for new home loans through our strategic partner, Aussie Home Loans that will exceed the lending of some of Australia's larger trading banks," Gill said. Aussie Home Loans is Australia's largest non-bank home loan lender.
"We also expect to remain very competitive on pricing. 1997 will see increased competition among lenders," Gill added.

The decision to raise funds offshore would allow PUMA to further diversify its funding base, spread funding risk and further reduce funding costs. These saving would be passed onto Australian borrowers, he added.
"The timing of our offshore issuance depends on market conditions and withholding tax considerations," Gill said.
PUMA has raised a total of A$3.508 billion in the Australian market since its first bond issue in June 1993.
